01

Setting specification

Task

Find an approximately stationary primal point for the Moreau envelope of the value function obtained by maximizing the average component payoff over the dual set.

$$ \Phi(x)=\max_{y\in Y}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x,y),\qquad\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}}\Phi(x). $$

Admissible model

The set $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$ is known, nonempty, compact, and convex, with $\operatorname{diam}(Y)\le D_Y$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$. Each $f_i$ is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of the product domain.

The objective $f=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i$ is concave in $y$ only after averaging; individual components need not be concave. Initialization satisfies $\Phi(x_0)-\inf_x\Phi(x)\le\Delta<\infty$ and need not be exactly dual-optimal.

$$ \frac1n\sum_i\|\nabla f_i(z)-\nabla f_i(w)\|_2^2\le\beta^2\|z-w\|_2^2\quad(\forall z,w). $$

Oracle interface

Public inputs include block dimensions $d_x,d_y$ and $D_Y$, $\Delta$, $\beta$, $\varepsilon$, $n$, together with the stated initial point and feasible geometry. Hidden analytic representations are not revealed.

$$ (i,x,y)\longmapsto(f_i(x,y),\nabla_x f_i(x,y),\nabla_y f_i(x,y)). $$

The algorithm selects $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$, and $y\in Y$. Component identities are fixed, repeated evaluations are charged again, and responses are exact noiseless real values.

Exact Euclidean projection onto the known set is allowed. Its calls are recorded separately and excluded from the primary query count.

Output

Return $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^{d_x}$.

The output may be any measurable postprocessing of the history, including an unqueried point, average, or convex combination. It must satisfy the stated domain and feasibility requirements; no additional function value or computable certificate is required.

Loss or accuracy criterion

The loss is the Euclidean norm of the Moreau envelope gradient of the reduced average payoff, evaluated at the returned primal point. The norm must be at most $\varepsilon$ with probability at least $2/3$.

$$ \|\nabla\Phi_{1/(2\beta)}(\widehat{x})\|_2 $$

$\Phi_{1/(2\beta)}(c)=\min_u\{\Phi(u)+\beta\|u-c\|_2^2\}$; $\nabla\Phi_{1/(2\beta)}(c)=2\beta(c-\operatorname{prox}_{\Phi/(2\beta)}(c))$. Neither the envelope gradient nor an inner proximal oracle is supplied.

Resource accounting

One bundled component-value and joint-gradient response costs one $N_{\rm component}$ call. A complete average-value or average-gradient scan costs $n$ calls.

Use a fixed worst-case budget: calls never exceed the prespecified $N$ on any instance or random execution path. Earlier stopping within the budget is permitted.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Arbitrary measurable sequential adaptive randomized algorithms are allowed. The private seed is independent of the hidden instance. Queries, stopping, and output may use the full history, without additional span, zero-respecting, communication, or memory restrictions.

A single algorithm is chosen from the public input and must satisfy the guarantee for every fixed admissible instance.

$$ \Pr\!\left(\|\nabla\Phi_{1/(2\beta)}(\widehat{x})\|_2\le\varepsilon\right)\ge\frac23. $$

Probability is over private algorithmic randomness only. The unknown instance is fixed before interaction.

Budget convention
fixed_worst_case_cap

Notation and parameters

$A$

The dimensionless scale of the initial primal objective gap.

Domain
Positive real number

$A=\beta\Delta/\varepsilon^2$

$A_\star$

Sufficient accuracy threshold in the source theorem; no numerical value is specified.

Domain
Universal positive constant
$B$

The dimensionless scale of the dual-domain diameter.

Domain
A nonnegative real.

$B=\beta D_Y/\varepsilon$

$\overline B$

Saturation scale unifying the small- and large-diameter regimes

Domain
At least one.

$\overline B=\max\{1,B\}$

$D_Y$

Euclidean diameter bound for the dual feasible domain

Domain
A nonnegative real.

$\operatorname{diam}(Y)=\sup_{u,v\in Y}\|u-v\|_2\le D_Y$

$\Delta$

A public bound on the initial reduced-objective value above its infimum. Attainment of the infimum is not required.

Domain
Positive real number

$\Phi(x_0)-\inf_x\Phi(x)\le\Delta$

$\beta$

Mean-square average Lipschitz upper bound for component joint gradients

Domain
Positive real number

$\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|\nabla f_i(z)-\nabla f_i(w)\|_2^2\le\beta^2\|z-w\|_2^2$

$d_x$

Primal-space dimension

Domain
Positive integer
$d_y$

The dimension of the dual-variable space.

Domain
Positive integer
$\ell$

A logarithmic factor in the upper bound for the large-diameter regime

Domain
Positive real number

$\ell=\log(2+n+A+B)$

$\varepsilon$

The Euclidean-norm tolerance for the reduced objective’s Moreau-envelope gradient.

Domain
Positive real number
$n$

Fixed number of finite-sum components; the full function or operator is their 1/n average

Domain
Positive integer
$\|\cdot\|_2,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$

Euclidean norm and inner product; the product-space norm is the square root of the sum of the squared block norms.

Domain
The specified finite-dimensional real vector space.

$\|v\|_2=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$

$f$

Unknown real-valued payoff, with primal and dual input blocks.

Domain
$f:(x,y)\mapsto f(x,y)\in\mathbb R$
$x,y,z$

Primal variable, dual variable, and joint point

Domain
$x\in\mathbb R^{d_x},\ y\in\mathbb R^{d_y},\ z=(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{d_x+d_y}$

$z=(x,y)$

$\nabla f,\nabla_x f,\nabla_y f$

Complete joint gradient and its two blocks

Domain
$\nabla_x f\in\mathbb R^{d_x},\ \nabla_y f\in\mathbb R^{d_y}$

$\nabla f=(\nabla_x f,\nabla_y f)$

$\Phi$

Reduced objective after global dual maximization; neither its value nor gradient is an additional free interface

Domain
Real-valued function on the primal-variable space

$\Phi(x)=\max_{y\in Y}f(x,y)$

$f_i,i$

The fixed ith real-valued component and the algorithm-selected index.

Domain
$i\in\{1,\ldots,n\},\quad f_i:\text{the declared product domain}\to\mathbb R$

$f=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n f_i$

$x_0,y_0$

The public initial primal and dual variables.

Domain
The respective feasible domains. Both equal zero when the origins are explicitly fixed.
$\widehat x$

The point or variable blocks ultimately returned by the algorithm, corresponding to the hatted variables in the error formula.

Domain
A feasible primal point in $\mathbb R^{d_x}$.
$\mathbb E,\Pr$

Expectation and probability over the explicitly allowed algorithm and sample randomness, with the hidden instance fixed.

Domain
Operations on the corresponding probability space

Number of bundled calls returning a selected component value and full joint gradient.

Domain

Projection count, uncharged in the primary query-cost projection

Domain

A uniform cap on principal information calls for every admissible instance and execution path.

$N^\star$

The infimum principal query budget among algorithms satisfying every stated instancewise output guarantee.

Natural logarithm and its nonnegative truncation

Domain
Arguments of log and ln are positive; the argument of $\log_+$ may be zero.

$\log_+(t)=\log(\max\{1,t\})$

$\Phi_{1/(2\beta)}$

The Moreau envelope of the $\beta$-weakly convex reduced objective; its gradient is used only for evaluation.

Domain
A differentiable real-valued function on $\mathbb R^{d_x}$.

$\Phi_{1/(2\beta)}(c)=\min_u\{\Phi(u)+\beta\|u-c\|_2^2\}$

$\operatorname{prox}_{\Phi/(2\beta)}$

The unique proximal minimizer defining the Moreau envelope; this interface is not supplied.

Domain
$\mathbb R^{d_x}\to\mathbb R^{d_x}$

$\operatorname{prox}_{\Phi/(2\beta)}(c)=\arg\min_u\{\Phi(u)+\beta\|u-c\|_2^2\}$

$Y$

Known nonempty compact convex dual domain with Euclidean diameter at most $D_Y$

Domain
$Y\subset\mathbb R^{d_y}$

Algorithms using the allowed interfaces, algorithm restrictions, and output domain, and satisfying the displayed complete error guarantee for every fixed admissible instance
